HOW TO PLAY
BEGINNER
Everything you need for your first run.
THE WHEEL
▲◄▼►SPACE

Steer with the arrows or A / D — one tap moves exactly one lane. Up and down slide you along the road.

Space is your ability. P or Escape pauses.

On touch: drag the road to steer, hold the energy bar for your ability.

HOW YOU DIE

One touch of anything ends the run — there is no health bar.

Traffic comes at you from ahead. Watch for blinkers: some drivers change lanes.

The road is never fully blocked. There is always a way through. Find it.

HOW YOU SCORE

Nothing is scored for just surviving. Points come from passing cars — and only cars in your lane or the ones right next to it. Distant lanes pay nothing.

Ordinary cars are worth points, trucks and reckless drivers , ambulances — all times your multiplier.

JUMP

Hold Space to jump. You fly over everything — even ambulances — for up to about 3 seconds. Release to land early.

Take-off needs of the bar's nine cells. Energy does not recharge on its own: earn it back by passing cars (+1 cell, trucks +2) and near misses (+4).

GETTING PAID

Coins are counted up at the end of each run — passes pay , trucks , ambulances , and anything you jump clean over pays five times more.

Your multiplier scales the final payout too. Spend it all in the GARAGE.

INTERMEDIATE
Scoring, abilities and where the money comes from.
THE MULTIPLIER
4.30x
AT 200 KM/H

Everything is multiplied. Fewer lanes pay more (3 lanes: x1.30). Harder difficulty pays more (SUICIDAL: x1.40). Bigger cars pay more — a Road Train nearly doubles a Stock car's rate.

And past 50 km/h, every extra km/h adds +1%. At 200 km/h that alone is x2.5. Speed is most of your score.

CLOSE CALLS

Shave past a car without touching it and you bank x multiplier, plus 4 cells of energy.

The faster you go, the more room counts as "close" — close calls get easier at speed. They don't count while jumping, and reversing into traffic pays nothing.

Two near misses fill a jump.

SHIELD BUMP

Nine heavy vehicles trade Jump for the ram. Tap Space: +40% speed and a front guard that smashes traffic aside — but only head-on. A side-swipe still kills you.

It runs at least 1 second, drains about a cell per second, and every kill refunds a little — trucks refund double. Chain them.

THE FAST WAY TO GET RICH

Six missions roll every midnight — the coin ones ladder up , so a full day pays . That is the fast lane to expensive cars; grinding runs is the slow lane.

You don't have to be good at the game to collect it — missions ask you to play, not to win. One good run a day also keeps your Daily Gift streak alive.

MASTER
Reading the road, and the trades good players make.
READ THE ROAD

Traffic spawns ahead — but ambulances hunt you from behind.

Ride low and you have maximum time to thread traffic, but the siren reaches you first. Ride high and passes bank earlier and ambulances take longest to catch you — but new traffic is in your face.

Pick your row for the problem in front of you. When a lane flashes red, that lane is cleared for a reason. Leave it, or jump.

THE AMBULANCE TRADE

An ambulance passed on the ground refills 5 cells — over half your bar, the best energy in the game.

Jumped over, it pays coins but only +1 cell.

Broke? Jump it. Low on energy? Hold your nerve and let it pass. Never spend a jump on one by reflex.

STAY CLOSE, STAY PAID

Passes only count within one lane of you. Hugging the thick of traffic scores; cruising an empty edge lane scores nothing.

Reckless drivers — about one in eight — never stop switching lanes. Treat any car with a blinker as already moving.

Breakdowns don't move at all, which makes them the fastest thing on the road. The flashing warning sign is your only notice.

PROGRESSION
Everything that carries over between runs.
THE MAIN MENU
HIGHWAYRECKLESSDRIVING

Only START RUN drives. Everything else is a tab, and this is all of them.

GARAGE — spend coins on cars, paint and boosters. SCORES — your best runs. AWARDS — achievements. STATS — the same runs as charts.

MISSIONS and GIFT are the daily rewards. SETTINGS holds sound and steering; lanes and difficulty now live on the menu itself, above START RUN, because both change your multiplier.

SPOTTING CARS

You cannot buy a car you have never seen.

Every car in the Garage also drives the road as ordinary traffic. The moment one is actually on screen it is discovered — you do not have to pass it, hit it or do anything at all — and its Garage tile turns from ??? into a real car with a price.

Rarer cars show up less often, so the Garage fills in slowly by itself. There are to find.

YOUR LEVEL

Points score you a run. The same points, before any multiplier, are also your XP.

So levelling rewards playing rather than playing well — a long clumsy run and a short brilliant one can be worth the same. Level 2 needs XP, and each level asks 50 more than the last.

Ten ranks of ten levels, Rust up to Diamond, then Champion past 100.

GIFTS, WORDS AND MISSIONS

Three things reset at midnight, and all three ask only that you play.

The Daily Gift unlocks once a run that day beats a score threshold that rises with your level — currently . Claiming it keeps your streak alive.

The Daily Word collects one letter at a time from gift rolls; finishing a word pays double. Missions give six goals a day, three paying coins and three paying XP.

PERFORMANCE SCORE
YOURS RIGHT NOW

One lucky run does not make you good, so the Scores screen does not rank you on one.

Your best runs are sorted, and each counts for 95% of the one above it — your best in full, the next at 95%, the one after at 90%, on down to a hundred runs.

A single huge score still moves it most, but a pile of consistent ones catches up. Beating an old run replaces it rather than adding to it.

ABOUT
Where this came from. Nothing here will help you drive.
WHERE IT CAME FROM

The idea is borrowed from those tiny driving games that came preloaded on old handsets — a few lanes, oncoming traffic, and one question: how long can you last?

No garage, no missions, no achievements. You drove until you didn't. This is that game, given somewhere to grow.

IT STARTED AS A CAPTCHA

Work began on 21 August 2026. The first version wasn't presented as a game at all — it was dressed up as one of those "prove you're human" boxes, complete with a fake browser frame and the instruction steer the car and don't crash.

The frame came off on day one and never went back on.

DRAWN IN CODE

There isn't a single image file in this game. Every car, every roadside tree, every coin is drawn rectangle by rectangle in code, then scaled up so the pixels stay sharp.

The music isn't a file either — it's generated while you play. The whole thing is one HTML file you could carry on a USB stick.

BY THE NUMBERS
405
BATCHES OF WORK

vehicles, kinds of scenery, and over twelve thousand lines in a single file.

Every change since day one is written down — what changed, why, and how it was checked. That log is now several times longer than the game itself.

THE PRICES ARE REAL

Every price tag in the garage is based on what the real vehicle costs. That's why a Formula 1 car runs to millions and a go-kart is pocket change.

It also means rarity and price don't always agree. A bin lorry outcosting a supercar isn't a bug — that's simply what they cost.
